title: Replicating CoT Monitoring on Summarization Tasks: Does Monitor Catch Faithful-Summary Manipulation?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: summarization is widely deployed and selective omission is a subtle manipulation. Demonstrating CoT monitoring effectiveness here broadens coverage. But the safety severity of summarization manipulation is lower than agentic sabotage.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Summarization datasets like XSum/CNN-DailyMail are available. Constructing incentivized omission prompts is feasible. Running a CoT monitor on summaries is straightforward. Medium compute sufficient. Beginner-accessible with mentor.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires constructing a dataset of incentivized omissions and labeling them, but the scale can be kept small. Two monitoring conditions (CoT vs. action-only). Manageable in 30 hours if dataset is kept to ~50-100 examples.
